question: The Indian National Science Academy is situated in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian National Science Academy (INSA) is headquartered in New Delhi. (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय विज्ञान अकादमी — नई दिल्ली)

 

• INSA was founded in 1935 (initially as the National Institute of Sciences of India, Calcutta) and was renamed and shifted to New Delhi in 1970.

 

• It is the premier science academy of India, functioning as the principal body representing Indian scientists across all fields of science and technology.

 

• INSA elects Fellows from among distinguished scientists and publishes research journals; it also administers several prestigious science awards and fellowships.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Indian science bodies include the Indian Academy of Sciences (Bengaluru), founded by C.V. Raman in 1934, and the National Academy of Sciences, India (Allahabad/Prayagraj), founded in 1930.

 

NOTE

 

• Hyderabad (Option 2): Home to institutions like CCMB and NGRI, but not INSA's headquarters.

 

• Allahabad (Option 3): Seat of the National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI), a different body from INSA.

 

• Bangaluru (Option 4): Seat of the Indian Academy of Sciences, again a distinct organisation from INSA.

question: 'The state shall endeavour to secure to all workers a living wage and and a decent standard of life'. Which of the following is correct about the given statement in the context of india ?
option_1: It is mentioned in the 43rd Article of the Constitution.
option_2: It is mentioned in the 44th Article of Constitution.
option_3: This is a Gandhian principle of Directive Principles of State Policy.
option_4: This is a liberal principle of Directive Principles of State Policy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is mentioned in the 43rd Article of the Constitution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 43 of the Indian Constitution, under Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy), directs the State to endeavour to secure to all workers a living wage and a decent standard of life. (जीवन निर्वाह मजदूरी — अनुच्छेद 43)

 

• Article 43 falls under the DPSPs, which are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts) but are fundamental in the governance of the country as per Article 37.

 

• Article 43 also provides for the promotion of cottage industries on an individual or cooperative basis in rural areas.

 

• Most standard classifications (e.g., by M.P. Jain and other constitutional scholars) place Article 43 among the Socialistic principles of the DPSPs, since it deals with labour welfare and economic justice, not among the Gandhian principles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 43A (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976) provides for workers' participation in management of industries.

 

• Article 43B provides for the promotion of co-operative societies and is classified as a Gandhian principle.

 

NOTE

 

• 44th Article (Option 2): Article 44 deals with a Uniform Civil Code, unrelated to workers' living wage.

 

• Gandhian principle (Option 3): Article 43 is generally classified as a Socialistic principle, not a Gandhian one (Gandhian principles include Articles 40, 43B, 46, 47, 48).

 

• Liberal-intellectual principle (Option 4): Liberal-intellectual principles (e.g., Articles 44, 45, 48, 50) deal with matters like uniform civil code, education and judiciary-executive separation, not labour welfare.

question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the Indian monsoon and the Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)?
option_1: The shift in the position of the ITCZ can influence the monsoon patterns in India.
option_2: ITCZ is located in the Indo-Gangetic plains during February.
option_3: The ITCZ is a phenomenon that occurs only during winter.
option_4: The ITCZ has no impact on the Indian monsoon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The shift in the position of the ITCZ can influence the monsoon patterns in India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is a low-pressure belt near the equator where the north-east and south-east trade winds converge. (अंतर-उष्णकटिबंधीय अभिसरण क्षेत्र — भारतीय मानसून)

 

• The apparent northward/southward shift of the ITCZ, following the sun's vertical movement, is a key factor controlling the onset and behaviour of the Indian monsoon — its northward shift over the Indo-Gangetic plains in summer is associated with the seasonal low that draws in the monsoon winds.

 

• This shifted, monsoon-season ITCZ over India is also referred to as the monsoon trough.

 

• The ITCZ is a year-round phenomenon, migrating seasonally with the sun, and is not confined to winter alone.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• In winter (including February), the ITCZ lies to the south of the Indian subcontinent, closer to the equator, not over the Indo-Gangetic plains.

 

• The withdrawal of the monsoon is associated with the southward retreat of the ITCZ and re-establishment of high pressure over north-west India.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2: During February (winter), the ITCZ lies well to the south, near/south of the equator — not over the Indo-Gangetic plains.

 

• Option 3: The ITCZ exists throughout the year, migrating seasonally; it is not a winter-only phenomenon.

 

• Option 4: The ITCZ's seasonal shift is, in fact, central to explaining the onset and strength of the Indian monsoon, so it is incorrect to say it has no impact.

question: Which country first introduced zero-based budgeting?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The US.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB) requires every expenditure to be justified afresh for each new budget period, starting from a "zero base", rather than simply adjusting the previous year's budget. (शून्य आधारित बजट — संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका)

 

• The concept was developed by Peter Pyhrr at Texas Instruments (USA) in the late 1960s/1970.

 

• It was first applied to government budgeting by Jimmy Carter, then Governor of Georgia, USA, and later introduced at the US federal government level in 1977 after Carter became President.

 

• ZBB was thus first introduced and popularised in the United States, both in the corporate and public sectors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In India, elements of zero-based budgeting were introduced in certain ministries/departments starting in 1987.

 

• ZBB is contrasted with incremental budgeting, where the previous year's allocations are simply adjusted upward or downward.

 

NOTE

 

• India (Option 1): Adopted zero-based budgeting later, from 1987 onward, not the country of origin.

 

• Germany (Option 2): Not associated with the origin of zero-based budgeting.

 

• The UK (Option 4): Not associated with the origin of zero-based budgeting.

question: The famous Rath Yatra, Car Festival is associated with which Lord?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Jagannath.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rath Yatra (Chariot/Car Festival) is celebrated annually at Puri, Odisha, in honour of Lord Jagannath, along with his siblings Balabhadra and Subhadra. (रथ यात्रा — भगवान जगन्नाथ)

 

• The deities are taken out in three massive, decorated wooden chariots from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple, about 3 km away.

 

• It is one of the oldest and largest chariot festivals in the world, observed in the Hindu month of Ashadha (June-July).

 

• The term "Juggernaut" in English is derived from the massive, unstoppable chariots of this festival.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The chariots of Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are called Nandighosa, Taladhwaja and Darpadalana respectively.

 

• Rath Yatra is also celebrated at other places associated with Jagannath temples, such as Ahmedabad and internationally by ISKCON.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Shiva (Option 1): Associated with festivals like Mahashivratri, not the Rath Yatra.

 

• Lord Indra (Option 3): Associated with the ancient Indra Dhwaja festival, not the Puri Rath Yatra.

 

• Lord Brahma (Option 4): Has very few dedicated festivals (e.g., at Pushkar) and is not linked to the Rath Yatra.

question: Which of the following is the main advantage of the import substitution policy?
option_1: It may make the indigenous industries more competitive.
option_2: It will help the consumers by providing them with unlimited choices.
option_3: It helps the nation achieve self-reliance.
option_4: It led to optimum allocation of resources.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It helps the nation achieve self-reliance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Import substitution is an economic policy under which a country replaces foreign imports with domestically produced goods, aiming to reduce dependence on other economies. (आयात प्रतिस्थापन नीति — आत्मनिर्भरता)

 

• Its main advantage is that it promotes self-reliance (Swadeshi/Atmanirbharta) by encouraging domestic production and reducing a country's dependence on foreign goods, especially for essential and strategic sectors.

 

• India adopted an import substitution industrialisation strategy, particularly from the 1950s to the 1980s, to build domestic industrial capacity behind tariff and licensing barriers.

 

• By protecting domestic industries from foreign competition, it also aims to conserve foreign exchange reserves.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Import substitution is often contrasted with an export promotion strategy, which focuses on producing for international markets rather than protecting the domestic market.

 

• Critics note that prolonged import substitution can lead to inefficiency and lack of competitiveness due to reduced exposure to foreign competition.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Protected industries, shielded from foreign competition, tend to become less, not more, competitive over time.

 

• Option 2: By restricting imports, consumers typically get fewer choices, not unlimited choices.

 

• Option 4: Protection from competition often leads to inefficient, not optimum, allocation of resources.

question: Who among the following Vijaynagar rulers married his daughter to Firuz Shah Bahmani?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Deva Raya I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Deva Raya I, ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire (Sangama dynasty), gave his daughter in marriage to the Bahmani Sultan Firuz Shah Bahmani (Tajuddin Firuz Shah) as part of a peace settlement after conflict between the two kingdoms. (देव राय प्रथम — फिरुज शाह बहमनी)

 

• This episode is linked to the events sometimes called the "War of the Goldsmith's Daughter", following which peace was made and the marriage alliance was arranged.

 

• Deva Raya I reigned in the early 15th century (c. 1406-1422 CE) and is also known for building irrigation dams/anicuts across the Tungabhadra river.

 

• Firuz Shah Bahmani ruled the Bahmani Sultanate from 1397 to 1422 CE, a contemporary and frequent rival of Vijayanagara.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vijayanagara-Bahmani rivalry over the Raichur Doab and Tungabhadra region continued across several generations of both dynasties.

 

• Krishna Deva Raya, of the later Tuluva dynasty, is most famous for his conflicts with, and victories over, the Bahmani successor sultanates (e.g., Battle of Raichur).

 

NOTE

 

• Deva Raya II (Option 1): Grandson/successor of Deva Raya I; known for military reforms including recruiting Muslim archers, not this marriage alliance.

 

• Krishna Deva Raya (Option 3): The most celebrated Vijayanagara ruler (Tuluva dynasty), known for the Battle of Raichur against the Bahmani successor states, not this episode.

 

• Bukka I (Option 4): Co-founder of the Vijayanagara Empire along with Harihara I, predates this event.

question: What is the most stable mineral during the process of weathering?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Quartz.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Goldich Dissolution/Stability Series, Quartz is the most resistant/stable mineral to chemical weathering among common rock-forming silicate minerals. (क्वार्ट्ज — सबसे स्थिर खनिज)

 

• This is because quartz has no cleavage planes and a fully polymerised (three-dimensional) silica tetrahedral structure with no weak metal-oxygen bonds to attack, making it highly resistant to chemical breakdown.

 

• Minerals that crystallise at higher temperatures (like olivine) from magma are generally least stable at the Earth's surface (Bowen's Reaction Series), while quartz, which crystallises last at lower temperatures, is most stable.

 

• Because of this stability, quartz survives weathering and transport, making it the dominant mineral in most sands and sandstones.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Goldich stability series (most to least stable): Quartz > Muscovite > K-feldspar > Biotite/Amphibole > Pyroxene > Ca-plagioclase > Olivine.

 

• This order is essentially the reverse of Bowen's Reaction Series of magma crystallisation.

 

NOTE

 

• Olivine (Option 2): The least stable/most easily weathered silicate mineral, as it crystallises first at the highest temperature from magma.

 

• Pyroxene (Option 3): More stable than olivine but far less stable than quartz in the weathering series.

 

• Amphibole (Option 4): More resistant than pyroxene and olivine but still much less stable than quartz.

question: Which project aims to develop state roads along coastal border areas, including connectivity of non-major ports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatmala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharatmala Pariyojana is an umbrella road and highway development programme of the Government of India, launched in 2017, under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. (भारतमाला परियोजना — तटीय एवं सीमा सड़कें)

 

• Among its components, Bharatmala includes the development of state roads in coastal areas and border areas, along with connectivity to non-major ports, to boost trade, tourism and strategic access.

 

• Its major components also include Economic Corridors, Inter-Corridor and Feeder Routes, National Corridor Efficiency Improvement, Border and International connectivity roads, Coastal and Port connectivity roads, and Green-field expressways.

 

• It subsumed earlier programmes like the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) and aims to optimise the efficiency of freight and passenger movement across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Golden Quadrilateral, launched in the late 1990s, connects the four metro cities Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata via four/six-lane highways.

 

• Setu Bharatam is a scheme aimed at making all national highways free of railway level crossings by constructing ROBs/RUBs and repairing old bridges.

 

NOTE

 

• Golden Quadrilateral (Option 1): Connects India's four major metro cities, not focused on coastal/border state roads.

 

• Setubharatam Pariyojana (Option 2): Focused on railway level-crossing-free national highways via bridges, not coastal border roads.

 

• District Headquarters Connectivity Scheme (Option 3): Aims to connect unconnected district headquarters to the national highway network, a different objective.

question: As per the newly released Surrogacy Rules 2022, surrogacy couples must purchase health insurance coverage for the surrogate mother for a period of _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is three years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Surrogacy (Regulation) Rules, 2022 (notified under the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021), intending couples/parents must purchase a general health insurance coverage for the surrogate mother for a period of 36 months (three years). (सरोगेसी नियम 2022 — तीन वर्ष का स्वास्थ्य बीमा)

 

• This insurance must cover the surrogate mother for postpartum delivery complications during this period.

 

• The Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021 permits only altruistic surrogacy (no monetary compensation beyond medical expenses/insurance) and bans commercial surrogacy in India.

 

• The Act is administered with State/District-level Surrogacy Boards overseeing registration of surrogacy clinics and compliance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under the Act, only a close relative of the intending married couple can act as a surrogate mother (in the original 2021 provisions), and the surrogate mother must be a married woman having a child of her own.

 

• The Act also mandates that surrogacy clinics/procedures require registration and certification from the appropriate authority.

 

NOTE

 

• four years (Option 2): Not the prescribed period; the Rules specify 36 months (three years).

 

• one year (Option 3): Too short; does not match the notified 36-month requirement.

 

• six years (Option 4): Exceeds the actual prescribed duration of three years.

question: In which year did India make its One-Day International (ODI) debut?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1974.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India played its first One-Day International (ODI) match on 13 July 1974 against England at Headingley, Leeds. (भारत का पहला वनडे — 1974)

 

• India lost this debut ODI to England.

 

• The first ODI in the world was played between Australia and England at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) in 1971, after a Test match was abandoned due to rain.

 

• India's ODI journey later saw major landmarks, including winning the 1983 Cricket World Cup in England, and multiple 50-over World Cup titles/finals since.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first-ever Test match was played much earlier, in 1932 against England at Lord's.

 

• India won its first ODI World Cup in 1983 under the captaincy of Kapil Dev, defeating the West Indies in the final.

 

NOTE

 

• 1971 (Option 1): The year of the first-ever ODI in the world (Australia vs England), not India's debut.

 

• 1975 (Option 3): The year of the first Cricket World Cup, held in England, in which India participated, but not India's ODI debut year.

 

• 1972 (Option 4): No ODI involving India was played in this year.

question: Which of the following institution has been accredited as National Implementing Entity for Adaptation Fund under United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NABARD.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) has been accredited as the National Implementing Entity (NIE) for the Adaptation Fund under the UNFCCC for India. (नाबार्ड — अनुकूलन कोष की राष्ट्रीय कार्यान्वयन एजेंसी)

 

• The Adaptation Fund was established under the Kyoto Protocol to finance concrete adaptation projects/programmes in developing countries vulnerable to climate change.

 

• As NIE, NABARD is responsible for appraising, approving, supervising and managing adaptation projects funded under this mechanism in India.

 

• NABARD also acts as the National Implementing Entity for other climate funds, including certain functions related to the Green Climate Fund processes in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD was established in 1982 on the recommendation of the B. Sivaraman Committee, as an apex development bank for agriculture and rural development in India.

 

• India's National Designated Authority (NDA) for the Green Climate Fund is the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).

 

NOTE

 

• ICAR (Option 1): The Indian Council of Agricultural Research coordinates agricultural research, not climate fund implementation.

 

• NIRD (Option 2): The National Institute of Rural Development focuses on rural development training and research, not climate finance.

 

• RBI (Option 4): India's central bank, regulates monetary policy and banking, not an Adaptation Fund implementing entity.

question: The decadal growth rate of India's population as per Census 2011 is __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 17.64%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, India's population grew from about 1.03 billion (2001) to about 1.21 billion (2011), registering a decadal growth rate of 17.64%. (2011 जनगणना — 17.64% दशकीय वृद्धि दर)

 

• This marked a decline from the decadal growth rate of 21.54% recorded in the previous decade (Census 1991-2001), indicating a slowing pace of population growth.

 

• As per Census 2011, India's population density was 382 persons per sq. km, and the sex ratio was 943 females per 1000 males.

 

• Uttar Pradesh was the most populous state and Bihar recorded the highest decadal growth rate among major states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after Independence, conducted under the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.

 

• India's literacy rate as per Census 2011 was 74.04% (82.14% for males and 65.46% for females).

 

NOTE

 

• 17.02% (Option 1): Does not match the official Census 2011 decadal growth figure.

 

• 16.54% (Option 2): Does not match the official Census 2011 decadal growth figure.

 

• 15.65% (Option 4): Does not match the official Census 2011 decadal growth figure.

question: Which natural bioactive water-soluble phenolic compound is present in Fruits, vegetables and grains with red, purple, blue or black hues?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anthocyanins.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Anthocyanins are natural, water-soluble flavonoid phenolic pigments responsible for the red, purple, blue and black colours seen in many fruits, vegetables and grains. (एंथोसायनिन — लाल, बैंगनी, नीला रंगद्रव्य)

 

• Common sources include blueberries, blackberries, red cabbage, black rice, jamun (Java plum), purple grapes and eggplant (brinjal) skin.

 

• They are well known for their strong antioxidant properties, helping to neutralise free radicals in the body.

 

• As bioactive compounds, anthocyanins are being studied for potential health benefits including anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular protective effects.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Coumarins are aromatic organic compounds found in plants like cinnamon and tonka beans, giving a sweet, hay-like fragrance, not primarily linked to red/purple/blue pigmentation.

 

• Quercetin and Naringenin are other flavonoids found in foods like onions and citrus fruits respectively, associated with yellow pigmentation rather than red/purple/blue/black hues.

 

NOTE

 

• Coumarins (Option 1): Associated with fragrance/flavour compounds, not the red-purple-blue-black pigmentation described.

 

• Quercetin (Option 3): A flavonoid found in onions, apples, etc., but not the pigment responsible for red/purple/blue/black colouration.

 

• Naringenin (Option 4): A flavonoid mainly found in citrus fruits (e.g., grapefruit), associated with bitterness, not this pigmentation.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct with respect to income or output?

i. Income or output are flows.

ii. Income or output are stocks.

iii. Income or output can be defined over a period.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only i and iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In economics, income (or output) is a flow variable, meaning it is measured per unit of time (e.g., per year), unlike a stock variable, which is measured at a point in time. (आय/उत्पादन — प्रवाह चर)

 

• Statement i is correct: Income/output is indeed a flow, since it accumulates or is generated over a defined time period.

 

• Statement iii is correct: Because it is a flow concept, income/output must always be defined with reference to a period (e.g., "income per annum"), not at a single instant.

 

• Statement ii is incorrect: Income/output is not a stock; stock variables (like wealth or capital) are measured at a specific point in time, not over a duration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples of stock variables in economics include wealth, capital, money supply (at a point in time), and inventory on a given date.

 

• Examples of flow variables include income, savings, investment, exports/imports, all measured over a period like a month or year.

 

NOTE

 

• Only ii and iii (Option 2): Incorrectly includes statement ii, since income/output is a flow, not a stock.

 

• Only i (Option 3): Leaves out the correct statement iii, which correctly notes that income/output is defined over a period.

 

• Only i and ii (Option 4): Incorrectly includes statement ii, which wrongly classifies income/output as a stock.

question: Which of these expressions is correct?
option_1: If the factor income from abroad is greater than the factor income paid abroad, then GNP would be greater than GDP.
option_2: If the factor income from abroad is greater than the factor income paid abroad, then GNP would be lower than GDP.
option_3: If the factor income earned from abroad is less than the factor income paid abroad, then GNP would be greater than GDP.
option_4: If the net factor income from abroad is negative, then GNP would be greater than GDP.
solution_text:
The correct answer is If the factor income from abroad is greater than the factor income paid abroad, then GNP would be greater than GDP.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The relationship between GNP (Gross National Product) and GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is: GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). (सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद — शुद्ध विदेशी कारक आय)

 

• NFIA = Factor income earned from abroad − Factor income paid abroad.

 

• If factor income earned from abroad exceeds factor income paid abroad, NFIA is positive, and since GNP = GDP + NFIA, GNP > GDP in this case.

 

• Conversely, if factor income paid abroad exceeds income earned from abroad, NFIA is negative, making GNP < GDP.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A country with more of its citizens/companies earning abroad than foreigners earning within it (e.g., due to large remittances/foreign investment income) typically has GNP > GDP.

 

• India generally has GNP slightly less than GDP in recent years, reflecting a negative NFIA due to foreign investment income outflows.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2: Incorrect — if income from abroad exceeds income paid abroad (positive NFIA), GNP is greater than, not lower than, GDP.

 

• Option 3: Incorrect — if income earned from abroad is less than income paid abroad, NFIA is negative, so GNP would be lower than, not greater than, GDP.

 

• Option 4: Incorrect — a negative NFIA means GNP would be lower than, not greater than, GDP.

question: Unit of frequency is _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is hertz.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The SI unit of frequency is the hertz (Hz), named after the German physicist Heinrich Rudolf Hertz. (हर्ट्ज — आवृत्ति की इकाई)

 

• Frequency is defined as the number of complete oscillations/cycles per second of a periodic wave or vibration.

 

• 1 hertz = 1 cycle per second; frequency is the reciprocal of the time period (T) of the wave, i.e., f = 1/T.

 

• Hertz is widely used to describe frequencies of sound waves, radio waves, AC electricity (e.g., 50 Hz mains supply in India), and computer clock speeds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Second (s) is the SI unit of time, not frequency.

 

• Gram (gm) is a unit of mass, and centimetre (cm) is a unit of length.

 

NOTE

 

• sec (Option 2): This is the unit of time period, the reciprocal of frequency, not frequency itself.

 

• gm (Option 3): This is a unit of mass, unrelated to frequency.

 

• cm (Option 4): This is a unit of length, unrelated to frequency.

question: Hariprasad Chaurasia plays which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Flute.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a world-renowned Indian classical musician celebrated for playing the bansuri (Indian bamboo flute). (हरिप्रसाद चौरसिया — बांसुरी वादक)

 

• He is credited with popularising the bansuri as a solo classical instrument, having earlier been used mainly for accompaniment/folk music.

 

• He has received major honours including the Padma Vibhushan (2000), Padma Bhushan (1992), and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

• He is closely associated with the Hindustani classical (Maihar gharana) tradition and has collaborated widely in Indian film and fusion music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other legendary flute (bansuri) exponents include Pandit Pannalal Ghosh.

 

• Famous tabla players include Ustad Zakir Hussain and Pandit Kishan Maharaj; a well-known Indian trumpet player is not typically featured in classical music circles.

 

NOTE

 

• Trumpet (Option 2): Not associated with Hariprasad Chaurasia; a primarily Western brass instrument.

 

• Tabla (Option 3): Associated with maestros like Zakir Hussain, not Chaurasia.

 

• Drum (Option 4): Not the instrument associated with Hariprasad Chaurasia.

question: Heating ethanol with excess concentrated sulphuric acid produces:
solution_text:
The correct answer is ethene.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Heating ethanol (C₂H₅OH) with excess concentrated sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) at about 170°C causes dehydration (removal of a water molecule), producing ethene (C₂H₄). (एथेनॉल का निर्जलीकरण — एथीन)

 

• The reaction is: C₂H₅OH → (conc. H₂SO₄, Δ) → C₂H₄ + H₂O.

 

• Here, concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a strong dehydrating agent, removing water from the alcohol molecule to form the alkene.

 

• This is a classic example of an elimination (dehydration) reaction used to prepare alkenes from alcohols in organic chemistry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• At lower temperatures (~140°C) with excess ethanol, concentrated sulphuric acid instead promotes intermolecular dehydration, forming diethyl ether.

 

• Concentrated sulphuric acid is also used as a catalyst and dehydrating agent in esterification reactions.

 

NOTE

 

• ethane (Option 1): A saturated alkane; not formed by dehydration of ethanol.

 

• ethyne (Option 2): An alkyne (C₂H₂); not obtained from this dehydration reaction.

 

• butane (Option 3): A four-carbon alkane; unrelated to this two-carbon dehydration reaction.

question: Who is referred to as 'Frontier Gandhi'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan, popularly known as 'Frontier Gandhi', was a prominent freedom fighter from the North-West Frontier Province (now in Pakistan). (सीमांत गांधी — खान अब्दुल गफ्फार खान)

 

• He founded the Khudai Khidmatgar ('Servants of God') movement, a non-violent movement against British rule, mainly among the Pashtun (Pathan) community.

 

• He was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and a firm believer in non-violence (ahimsa), which earned him the title "Frontier Gandhi".

 

• He was honoured with India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna, in 1987 — the first non-Indian citizen to receive it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ashfaqullah Khan was a revolutionary associated with the Kakori Conspiracy (1925), executed in 1927.

 

• Rajkumar Shukla was the peasant leader who persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to visit Champaran, Bihar, leading to the Champaran Satyagraha (1917).

 

NOTE

 

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 1): First President of India, a prominent Congress leader from Bihar, not called 'Frontier Gandhi'.

 

• Ashfaqullah Khan (Option 3): Revolutionary freedom fighter of the Kakori case, not associated with this title.

 

• Rajkumar Shukla (Option 4): Associated with the Champaran Satyagraha, not this title.

question: India won ________ medals in the International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF)'s world cup 2022, which was held in Cairo, Egypt.

• India's medal haul included performances from shooters such as Rhythm Sangwan and Anish Bhanwala, who won gold on the final day of the event.

 

• This World Cup was significant as it came ahead of major upcoming events like the Asian Games and Olympic qualification tournaments, showcasing India's growing strength in shooting sports.

 

• India topped the medal table ahead of established shooting nations, reflecting the depth of its shooting talent pool.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ISSF (International Shooting Sport Federation) is the world governing body for Olympic shooting sports (rifle, pistol and shotgun events).

 

• India also performed strongly at the ISSF World Championship 2022 (also held in Cairo, Egypt later that year), finishing second with 34 medals overall.

 

NOTE

 

• 5 (Option 1): Understates India's actual medal count of 7 at this event.

 

• 8 (Option 2): Overstates India's actual medal count of 7 at this event.

 

• 6 (Option 4): Understates India's actual medal count of 7 at this event.

question: Who among the following Indian shooters won the gold at the International Shooting Sport Federation's President's cup 2022?

• Indian shooter Rudrankksh Patil won the gold medal in the men's 10m air rifle event at the ISSF President's Cup 2022, held in Cairo, Egypt. (रुद्रांक्ष पाटिल — आईएसएसएफ प्रेसिडेंट्स कप 2022)

 

• The ISSF President's Cup is a season-ending, invitational shooting event featuring the top-ranked shooters from across the world in each event.

 

• Rudrankksh Patil had earlier become the 10m air rifle World Champion at the ISSF World Championship 2022, also held in Cairo.

 

• His win at the President's Cup further cemented his position as one of the top young shooting talents from India in the 10m air rifle category.

• The ISSF President's Cup brings together the best-performing shooters of the year based on world rankings across various ISSF events.

 

• India has produced several top shooters across categories, including in pistol events (Arjun Babuta - rifle) and shotgun events.

question: Who among the following personalities won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2021 for contribution to Manipuri Dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thokchom Ibemubi Devi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thokchom Ibemubi Devi was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for the year 2021 for her contribution to Manipuri dance. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार 2021 — मणिपुरी नृत्य)

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) is India's highest award given to practising artists in the fields of music, dance and drama, conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance and Drama.

 

• The awards for the years 2019, 2020 and 2021 were announced together and presented in a combined ceremony due to the COVID-19 pandemic-related delay.

 

• Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, known for its graceful, fluid movements and themes drawn from Vaishnavite traditions (Raas Leela).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in 1952 and is headquartered in New Delhi; it is the first National Akademi of the arts set up by the Republic of India.

 

• The Award carries a Tamrapatra (bronze plaque), an Angavastram, and a cash prize.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhuvan Kumar (Option 1): Not the recipient of the 2021 award for Manipuri dance.

 

• Sruti Bandopadhyay (Option 3): An Odissi dance exponent/institution builder, not the 2021 Manipuri dance awardee.

 

• Kumkum Dhar (Option 4): Not the recipient of the 2021 award for Manipuri dance.

question: Liberty, Equality and Fraternity slogan of ________ finds an echo in the Preamble of Indian Constitution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is French Revolution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity, enshrined in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution, are directly inspired by the slogan of the French Revolution (1789): "Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité". (स्वतंत्रता, समानता, बंधुत्व — फ्रांसीसी क्रांति)

 

• The Preamble declares India's resolve to secure to all its citizens Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity.

 

• The Indian Constitution's framers, particularly Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, drew on these Enlightenment-era ideals of the French Revolution while drafting the Preamble.

 

• The French Revolution (1789-1799) overthrew the monarchy and promoted principles of popular sovereignty and human rights that influenced constitutions worldwide, including India's.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term "Socialist" and "Secular" were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

 

• The concept of a Preamble as an introduction/summary of a constitution's objectives was itself borrowed from the Constitution of the USA.

 

NOTE

 

• Mexican Revolution (Option 1): A 20th-century socio-political revolution in Mexico, not the source of this specific slogan.

 

• Greek War of Independence (Option 2): A 19th-century struggle for Greek independence from Ottoman rule, unrelated to this slogan.

 

• American Declaration of Independence (Option 3): Inspired the idea of "fundamental rights" and the Preamble's structural concept, but the specific "Liberty, Equality, Fraternity" slogan originates from the French Revolution.

question: Which of the following dance forms originating in Kerala, is a solo recital by women?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form that originated in Kerala, traditionally performed as a solo dance by women. (मोहिनीअट्टम — केरल की एकल स्त्री नृत्य शैली)

 

• The name means "dance of the enchantress", referring to Lord Vishnu's Mohini avatar; it is characterised by graceful, swaying body movements.

 

• It is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, along with Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi, Kuchipudi, Manipuri and Sattriya.

 

• Mohiniyattam draws on both the Lasya (graceful, feminine) style and elements of both Bharatanatyam and Kathakali traditions, and its music follows the Carnatic style.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathakali, also from Kerala, is a male-dominated, elaborately costumed dance-drama form, not a solo women's recital.

 

• The Mohiniyattam form was revived and popularised in the 20th century with support from poet Vallathol Narayana Menon, founder of the Kerala Kalamandalam.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 2): A classical dance form originating in Odisha, not Kerala.

 

• Kathakali (Option 3): Also from Kerala, but is a dance-drama traditionally performed by men, not a solo women's recital.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 4): A classical dance form originating in Andhra Pradesh, not Kerala.
